name: Japan, Worked Out.
subtitle: A decision manual for your first trip.
thesis: Most first trips to Japan are two cities, one Shinkansen leg and a fortnight of day trips — which means a lot of the advice you have read, starting with "buy the rail pass", is priced for a trip you are not taking.

hooks.route-sequencing: Two bases beats four every time, but the day-trip-versus-relocate call is where a whole travel day quietly disappears — the guide works out which side each city falls on.
hooks.jr-pass-economics: The national pass needs about four long journeys to pay for itself and your trip probably has two; the guide shows the arithmetic before you spend ¥50,000 on a reflex.
hooks.ic-card-transit: A US-issued Visa will not top up a mobile Suica — Mastercard and Amex will — and discovering that at a Shinjuku gate costs you an afternoon; the guide sets the card up before you fly.
hooks.seasonal-timing: Golden Week and Obon do not just raise prices, they change which trip is possible — the guide names the weeks worth moving and the ones that are fine.
hooks.ryokan-onsen: The ryokan worth the splurge books out first and the tattoo rule is not negotiable at most onsen; the guide picks which city to spend that night in.

no_hook.cash-access: DEMOTED by the cold mine — only 1 article and 921w of money-and-costs corpus behind it. Surfaces fall back to the thesis. Either write 2-3 more cash/ATM articles or retire the swamp.
